title: Food spending more than doubles the week they host Thanksgiving

life.summary: Office manager on a salary, married, two kids (6 and 10), hosting Thanksgiving for 12 this year; shares a joint checking account with her partner for the house

known.fact: Her partner is off Wednesday to Friday and has the kids while school is closed
Shares a joint checking account with her partner for the house
Routine: a big grocery run on Saturday mornings and small top-ups on weeknights after work
known.source: learned from 8 weeks of bank history

known.fact: Routine: works 8 to 4:30 at the office, Monday to Friday

timeline.label: Sunday at home with the family
Her in-laws head home after breakfast

attached.label: Told Dev: 'We're hosting Thanksgiving this year, 12 people'
Usual food spending: about $210 a week (8 weeks to Nov 15)
School closed Wed Nov 25 to Fri Nov 27

best_fix.what: Say nothing about this week's food spending and nothing about the school closure.
best_fix.why: The jump ($490.74 on food and drink since Saturday, against about $210 in a usual week) is the Thanksgiving she told Dev about two weeks ago, it's one week, and it follows her usual pattern (the Saturday run plus weeknight top-ups), just bigger. The mortgage on Dec 1 is covered by the $3,290.48 in checking without counting the Dec 4 paycheck. The school closure is covered too: her partner is off Wednesday to Friday and she works only Wednesday morning.

must_not: Send a food spending alert or compare this week with a usual week
